title: Beginning of the war in Guinea
summary: The PAIGC attacked the barracks at Tite, south of Bissau, on 23 January 1963, opening the armed struggle in Portuguese Guinea. Guinea was the smallest of the three fronts and the one the Portuguese army came closest to losing: by the late 1960s the PAIGC held or contested most of the countryside, ran administration in the areas it held, and had support across the borders in Senegal and Guinea-Conakry. It was in Guinea that António de Spínola commanded, and the conclusions he drew there became Portugal e o Futuro in 1974. It is in the atlas as the front whose course did most to convince Portuguese officers that the war could not be won.
